title: The complete regular two-radius chart is an exact open rectangle

pre_flight.problem_match: Replace the noncompact p-to-one, b-to-infinity presentation left by K1750 with coordinates that expose every remote and singular boundary before whole-domain certification.
pre_flight.rederived_inputs: Use only K1731 variance normalization and u=3-m4; do not assume K1751 or a numerical optimizer.
pre_flight.collision_search: K1731 gives the p,a chart and K1749 handles two named sections, but no K1726--K1750 artifact contains the c,z rectangularization.

chart.round_trip: For every regular symmetric unit-variance two-radius law, c=p(1-a)^2/(1-p)>0 and z=1-a recover p,a,b exactly.
chart.moment_identity: p a+(1-p)b=1 and p a^2+(1-p)b^2=1+c, hence u=2-c.
chart.bijection: The formulas give a bijection between the regular u>q two-radius chart and the open rectangle (0,2-q)x(0,1).

scope_guard: This is an exact chart theorem for symmetric unit-variance two-radius four-point laws. It is not a Fisher minimization, all-seed theorem, or physical result.

post_flight.strongest_overclaim: A compact rectangular parameter closure does not make the Fisher objective continuous on every boundary or certify a minimum.
post_flight.strongest_counterexample_seam: The z-to-zero rare-atom face and joint z-to-zero, c-to-(2-q) corner remain analytically nonuniform.
post_flight.reproducibility_seam: The producer replays both directions with exact rational arithmetic and checks variance and u identities independently.
